questions.q: Why is lack of sustained executive sponsorship frequently cited as a top reason governance programs fail?
options: Roles like owner and steward only carry real organizational authority when someone senior enough visibly backs them
Executive sponsors are legally required to sign every data policy personally
It has no real impact — governance programs succeed or fail purely on technical merit
Executive sponsors are responsible for writing every quality rule themselves
questions.explain: Without visible senior backing, roles the program depends on don't get treated as legitimate or prioritized by the rest of the organization.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four ongoing things a real executive sponsor does, per this lesson?
options: Personally writes every data quality rule for every domain
Aligns governance with business strategy
Secures budget and resources
Breaks ties at the top when the governance committee can't resolve something
questions.explain: Writing individual quality rules is steward/custodian-level work. The sponsor's job is strategic alignment, resourcing, modeling behavior, and top-level escalation.

questions.q: What is the key difference between initial sponsorship and sustained sponsorship?
options: Sustained sponsorship means ongoing, renewed backing over time, not a one-time approval
There is no real difference between the two
Initial sponsorship always lasts longer than sustained sponsorship
Sustained sponsorship means the sponsor no longer needs to be named publicly
questions.explain: Getting an initial yes is the easy part; programs stall when that backing quietly erodes instead of being renewed each cycle.

questions.q: Which of these is a sign that executive sponsorship has become 'in name only'?
options: Nobody outside the governance team can name who the sponsor actually is
The sponsor attends every committee meeting and makes real decisions
The program's budget is renewed every cycle without a fight
The sponsor regularly discusses the program in strategy meetings
questions.explain: If the sponsor's involvement is invisible to the rest of the organization, the sponsorship isn't functioning as a real governance role.

questions.q: In Chapter 3's structure, where does an executive sponsor typically sit relative to the governance committee?
options: Above it — often the final escalation point when the committee itself can't resolve something
Below individual data stewards
Entirely outside the governance structure with no connection to it
As a rotating role held by a different data consumer each month
questions.explain: The sponsor sits above the committee as the top-level escalation point and the source of strategic backing and resourcing.
